reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown read 1 Chronicles' 'sons of Manasseh' as descendants rather than immediate sons, keeping Zelophehad within the Hepher line a generation further removed.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Who was Zelophahad's father?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/zelophehad.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: the daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh
sides.verseText: Then drew near the daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of Manasseh the son of Joseph; and these are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah.

sides.snippet: and the name of the second was Zelophehad: and Zelophehad had daughters
sides.verseText: and Machir took a wife of Huppim and Shuppim, whose sister's name was Maacah; and the name of the second was Zelophehad: and Zelophehad had daughters.
